newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian Democrats seek to keep sugar tariff.
newsitem.headline: Australian Democrats seek to keep sugar tariff.

text.p: The Australian Democrats, a key force in the Australian parliament's upper house, said on Thursday they would seek to quash government efforts to scrap the sugar tariff.

Democrats rural spokesman John Woodley urged disaffected members of the National Party, the junior member of the ruling coalition, to cross the floor and vote with the Democrats and the Labor opposition in the Senate to maintain the tariff.
Woodley said the Democrats would move an amendment to government legislation abolishing the A$55-a-tonne tariff when the measure was introduced in the Senate later this year.
The amendment would maintain the tariff and freeze it at its current level, with any future reductions tied to tariff cuts by other countries.
"You can't just rip away the sugar industry's principal support mechanism without appropriate adjustment measures in its place," Woodley said.
"The Democrats won't support exposing canegrowers to brutal competition from overseas producers who are still protected by tariffs."
The Liberal-National government has announced it would scrap the tariff from July 1.
But some National MPs have expressed deep concern about the decision.
The government does not have a majority in the upper house Senate and has relied on two independent senators for support to pass criticial legislation.
The government move to abolish the tariff would fail if two senators -- independents or disaffected Nationals -- joined the Democrats and the opposition to vote against it.
